ov: A North American omnivore with dexterous front paws, a black face mask and a ringed tail. Its most important sense is touch, through extremely sensitive front paws.

why.dg: It can carry rabies, and a roundworm found in about 60% of adults can cause fatal brain damage in people.
why.ac: Usually nocturnal; young raccoons forage with their mother at night.
why.et: Eaten in some areas, and hunted mostly for fur.

rg: North America, and since the mid-20th century also central Europe, the Caucasus and Japan, from escapes and introductions.
df: Usually nocturnal and omnivorous: about 40% invertebrates, 33% plants and 27% vertebrates.

cf.tip: A raccoon dog is a fox-like wild dog from East Asia, named for its raccoon-like face markings. It’s most closely related to foxes.

fx: Wild raccoons live only 1.8–3.1 years on average, though captive ones have passed 20.
